observed_vs_expected: The expected peak in best_target_score upon defect convergence to the half-wave condition was not sustained. The score rose quickly in rounds 1–2 (0.7005 → 0.7613), peaked in round 3 (0.7731), and then plateaued through rounds 4–5 (0.7610 → 0.7653). The tightest_margin remained static at 0.4494, indicating insufficient visible-band rejection. Additionally, the defect layer thickness did not approach the theoretical half-wave value, meaning the anticipated distinct telecom-band transmittance peak failed to form robustly.
deviation_mechanism: Physical resonance condition mismatch. The center defect layer (index 10) converged to ~200–204 nm physical thickness across the final four candidates. For a standard telecommunication dielectric (refractive index n ≈ 1.45–1.50), a first-order half-wave optical cavity at 1550 nm requires an optical thickness of 775 nm, translating to a physical thickness of ~515–535 nm. The optimizer settled approximately 330 nm below this threshold, trapping the solution in a shallow local minimum. Without satisfying the λ/2 condition, the Fabry-Pérot mode cannot achieve high Q-factor, capping the transmittance peak and preventing further score improvement despite additional optimization cycles.
continue_rationale: Five rounds have been executed with clear evidence of search stagnation, but the cause is physically correctable rather than fundamental. The plateau in best_target_score (0.7610–0.7653 over rounds 4–5) directly correlates with the defect layer thickness clustering at ~200 nm. Because the underlying design topology remains viable and the optimizer simply lacks the initialization guidance to cross the potential barrier toward the true resonance basin, a targeted structural adjustment is scientifically warranted to recover performance.
